record.paper_title: Some open problems related to small divisors
record.context_brief: Wandering domains near circular planetary orbits
record.original_question: In the planetary small-mass regime where one mass m0=1 and the other masses are sufficiently small, do wandering domains exist in every neighborhood of distinct coplanar circular orbits around the dominant mass, all moving in the same direction?

evidence.quote: Problem 3.3.2 (M. Herman) If one of the masses mo = 1 and all the other masses mj < < 1 are sufficiently small, are there wandering domains in any neighborhood of fixed distinct circular orbits around the mass mo and moving in the same direction in a plane?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider the Newtonian N-body problem in the plane with one dominant mass $m_0 = 1$ at the origin and $N-1$ further bodies of masses $m_1, \dots, m_{N-1} > 0$. Fix $N-1$ pairwise distinct positive radii $r_1, \dots, r_{N-1}$ and consider, for $m_0 = 1$ and $m_j$ sufficiently small ($1 \le j \le N-1$), the Keplerian limit in which each body $j$ moves on a circular orbit of radius $r_j$ around $m_0$, all orbits being coplanar and traversed in the same direction. View the dynamics on phase space (with the center of mass and total linear momentum reduced) and let $W$ denote any open neighborhood of the set of phase-space points corresponding to such configurations of distinct coplanar concentric circular orbits with common direction.

A wandering domain for a flow $\Phi^t$ on a phase space is a non-empty open set $U$ such that the sets $\Phi^{t}(U)$, $t \in \mathbb{R}$, are pairwise disjoint for an unbounded sequence of times (equivalently, $U$ is contained in the wandering set of $\Phi^t$).

Question: For all sufficiently small $m_1, \dots, m_{N-1}$, does every neighborhood $W$ as above contain a wandering domain of the planetary N-body flow?
artifact.status_search_result: Herman's question about the existence of wandering domains arbitrarily close to coplanar concentric circular orbits in the planetary regime is broadly cited as open. Related advances (e.g., Newhouse domains and oscillatory motions in the restricted 3-body problem, KAM-stability results for the planetary problem) address neighboring questions but do not resolve the existence of wandering domains in every neighborhood of the circular Keplerian orbits.

status_evidence.title: Coorbital homoclinic and chaotic dynamics in the Restricted 3-Body Problem
status_evidence.snippet: Discusses Newhouse domains and chaotic dynamics in restricted 3-body settings, related to Herman-type questions but not resolving the planetary wandering-domain problem.
status_evidence.claim: Related chaotic phenomena are established in restricted settings; the general planetary wandering-domain question remains unresolved.
